title: Exclusive | AI-Computing Startup Lambda Is Raising $4 Billion in Final Round Before Planned IPO
key_facts: Lambda is raising up to $4 billion at a $14.5 billion pre-money valuation; Coatue Management and Blackstone are leading (WSJ).
Could be its last private round before a planned 2027 IPO; the IPO was reportedly meant for this year but was pushed back amid market uncertainty.
Backlog grew from $15 billion in June to $50 billion in September, per a letter to investors seen by the Journal.
Much of the increase appears to come from a $35 billion commitment from Anthropic, signed in late August.
Lambda raised an additional $1 billion of debt last week.
Nscale, a British neocloud, filed for an IPO last month.
quote_evidence: Cloud provider Lambda is raising up to $4 billion at a $14.5 billion pre-money valuation, marking what could be its last private round before a planned 2027 IPO, according to The Wall Street Journal.
That means Lambda's valuation, which has climbed significantly since its 2025 funding round, could be leaning heavily on Anthropic's ability to keep paying.
why_it_matters_hint: Big pre-IPO round for an AI-computing supplier whose backlog leans on one customer.
notes: WSJ paywalled; read TechCrunch's account of the WSJ exclusive. The TechCrunch comment on Anthropic dependence is TechCrunch's analysis, labelled as such in the summary.
